source.title: Investigating the impact of low to moderate level label noise on Neural Network grokking dynamics

page_placements.theme: Generalization and memorization have setting-dependent timescales

record.file_problem: none; the supplied article text appears complete.
record.tranche_reason: Extends label-noise experiments to grokking on modular addition with an MLP, and reports training and test dynamics across noise levels.
record.gate_note: The paper reports grokking metrics under label noise, not zero training error and chance test error on image datasets with fully random labels. Its results bear on V4's broad noisy-label behavior in this algorithmic task and V2's training-time scaling. The random-label memorization statement in Related Work is cited prior work, not a study result.
record.test_reason: The sample trajectories report time to 95% training accuracy under 0%, 5% and 10% label corruption, bearing narrowly on V2's slowing of training convergence. The extracted rows instead measure time to generalization, which cannot establish training-fit speed or V4's final training/test-error pattern.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate for the main experiment: the authors conclude that label noise increases grokking time and integrated accuracy/loss gaps approximately exponentially, with all main runs eventually grokking. Qualify robustness: only configurations successfully inducing grokking retain the reported exponential pattern; several ablations show failures or irregular dynamics. The indices measure cumulative gaps, not necessarily larger final errors.
record.recipe_differences: Trains an embedding MLP on modular addition with uniform corruption of a subset of training labels and measures grokking, not image classifiers trained on fully random labels. Uses AdamW with weight decay 1.0, a 40/60 split, and fixed task-specific architecture.
record.method_sensitivity: Absolute grokking metrics and scaling exponents vary with weight decay and learning rate; the paper reports extreme or non-convergent behavior for several ablation settings. Three data partitions show differing magnitudes while retaining exponential trends.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean time to grok increases from 588 epochs without noise to 12509 at 15% noise; the fitted exponential trend has R²=0.855. All main runs meet the study's grokking thresholds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Low-to-moderate label corruption delays generalization after training accuracy reaches 95% in this modular-addition MLP configuration.

fits_no_version.finding: Integrated accuracy and loss gaps increase with noise; split validation retains the trend, while some hyperparameter configurations show irregular behavior or fail to grok within 50000 epochs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Noise-related grokking delay and cumulative generalization gaps depend on optimization settings.

record.problems: Five runs per noise level; the authors note local non-monotonicity and increasing variability at higher noise. The study uses one algorithmic task and one architecture family, with clean test labels. It does not directly measure random-label training error or chance test error. Hyperparameter ablation includes failed-to-converge and extreme cases.
record.rows_left_out: None; kept one row for every main-experiment noise level in Table 11. Split validation and hyperparameter-ablation rows were not extracted because the 60-row cap was not exceeded, but required main noise-level coverage was prioritized; those additional experiments likewise report grokking metrics and would provide further setting-level outcomes.

untested.parts: Completely random training labels, zero or near-zero training error, and chance test performance with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Time to zero or near-zero training error on completely random versus true labels; the small constant-factor claim. Sample threshold-crossing times do not establish aggregate convergence scaling.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit across corruption levels and steadily increasing final test error toward chance; corruption above 15%.
Whether explicit regularization prevents fully random-label fitting, and whether removing it impairs true-label generalization. The ablations measure grokking instead.
Separate learning trajectories for clean and corrupted examples establishing signal learning before noise memorization. Training preceding test generalization does not establish this ordering.

missing.what: Add training-threshold timing rows for the sample runs: 95% training accuracy at epochs 334, 363 and 412 under 0%, 5% and 10% noise. Keep these distinct from the later generalization endpoints and identify them as illustrative runs.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V2 and V4 limits_scope verdicts conflate delayed generalization with training-fit speed and final error behavior. Missing measurements and the restricted corruption range are untested parts, not evidence against those versions. No supplied result establishes perfect noisy-label memorization, and the 95% threshold does not rule it out.

versions.untested_parts: No fully random labeling experiment on training images; no test-error-at-chance result; no comparison of random versus true labels using unchanged settings.
Measures total epochs until grokking, not training time relative to a true-label baseline as a small constant factor.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Tests uniform random label corruption only from 0% to 15% on modular addition; does not test corruption through 100% or report perfect training accuracy at every level.
No random-label fitting comparison with weight decay, dropout or data augmentation; dropout is disabled in the principal configuration.
Does not measure whether real patterns are learned before memorizing noisy or random labels.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Grokking epochs rise substantially overall but are locally non-monotonic; the paper reports an exponential fit for aggregate trends, not a small constant-factor comparison with true-label fitting (R1–R31).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Main configuration, 0%–15% uniform label noise on modular addition
reader_labels.reason: All runs reportedly grokked, but test performance only reached within 5% of training accuracy, corruption stopped at 15%, and local epoch metrics are non-monotonic; the study does not establish perfect training fit at each corruption level or a steady test-error rise to chance (R1–R31).
